item.text:
**3B.3 Research Note: Olaf Scholz in 2024**

**Assessment:** I found **no reliable evidence** that Scholz personally incited hatred, revenge, dehumanization, scapegoating, or violence against minorities, migrants, journalists, or civil society in 2024. The record is mostly the opposite: public anti-hate messaging, defense of democratic pluralism, and condemnation of attacks. The main counterweight is that he hardened on deportations after violent attacks, but that rhetoric stayed framed around **violent criminals and legal status**, not ethnic or religious dehumanization.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| **Against hatred – For humanity and order** | Bundesregierung | 20 Jan 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/kanzler-kompakt-against-hatred-for-humanity-and-order-2254034 | Scholz explicitly urged unity, tolerance, and opposition to right-wing extremism, saying extremists attack democracy and that Germany’s large migrant-background population should be defended as part of the country. This is direct anti-incitement evidence. | **3B.3**, also **3B.2** |
| **Olaf Scholz condemns attacks on politicians after third assault in a week** | The Guardian | 8 May 2024 | https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/may/08/olaf-scholz-condemns-attacks-on-politicians-after-third-assault-in-a-week | Scholz condemned assaults on elected officials as outrageous and cowardly and pushed for greater protection. This is evidence against personal incitement or legitimization of political violence. | **3B.3**, also **3B.2** |
| **Scholz mahnt mehr Meinungsvielfalt in Medien an** | Reuters / onvista | 3 Jun 2024 | https://www.onvista.de/news/2024/06-03-scholz-mahnt-mehr-meinungsvielfalt-in-medien-an-0-20-26278418 | Scholz argued for more factual reporting and more diversity in newsroom voices, including more women, East Germans, and people with migrant backgrounds. This cuts against hostility toward journalists or exclusionary rhetoric. | **3B.3** |
| **German leader hardens on deportations amid row with far right as EU election looms** | Reuters / The Guardian | 6 Jun 2024 | https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/jun/06/scholz-hardens-line-on-deportations-after-row-with-far-right-as-german-election-looms | Scholz backed deporting violent foreign-born criminals, including people from Syria and Afghanistan, after a major attack. This is the closest counterweight, but it is law-and-order rhetoric, not dehumanization or ethnic scapegoating. | **3B.3** |
| **Germany's Scholz promises more deportations after visiting mass stabbing scene** | Reuters / Investing.com | 26 Aug 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/germanys-scholz-vows-tougher-asylum-rules-after-suspected-islamist-attack-3586443 | After Solingen, Scholz promised more deportations for those not allowed to stay in Germany. Again, this is hardline migration policy, but the target is unauthorized residence and violent offenders, not a group-inciting message against migrants as such. | **3B.3** |
| **Scholz: Viele geflüchtete Syrer sollten in Deutschland bleiben** | Reuters / onvista | 13 Dec 2024 | https://www.onvista.de/news/2024/12-13-scholz-viele-gefluechtete-syrer-sollten-in-deutschland-bleiben-0-20-26340369 | Scholz said integrated Syrians with jobs should be welcome to stay, while those without legal status, especially criminals, should leave. This is strong counterevidence to blanket scapegoating of refugees or ethnic/religious groups. | **3B.3** |

**Search gap**
- I did **not** find credible 2024 evidence of Scholz personally using dehumanizing, revenge, or hate-inciting language against minorities, migrants, journalists, civil society, or ethnic/religious groups.
- The available evidence is mostly **anti-hate** or **hardline but bounded** migration enforcement.
- The closest negative material is his post-attack deportation rhetoric, but it does **not** rise to personal incitement or group dehumanization on the sources I found.
